verdict.summary: You can use a General OAuth app. Each user connects and approves access to their own Zoom data. Public and unlisted external apps go through Marketplace review. Prepare test and security materials.
verdict.activeEffort: 2–4 days, mostly building secure OAuth, test access, and review materials (estimate)
verdict.mainGate: Public and unlisted external apps need Marketplace review before external distribution.

recommendation.text: Create a General OAuth app with user-managed access. Use unlisted external distribution unless Marketplace discovery matters. Each person then connects only their own Zoom data.

sources.quote: User-managed: Individual users add and manage the app. The app has access to only the user's authorized data.
Unlisted apps might be a preferable option for you if you want to limit access to your app and don't want it available to the general public.

scopeTiers.text: Read a connected person's meetings. This is the cheapest useful tier and needs normal Marketplace review.

sources.quote: User-managed apps can only request scopes that allow access to an individual user's associated data.
The Marketplace Security Review Team verifies that the app only requests the minimum necessary OAuth scopes required for its functionality.

scopeTiers.text: Create or change a connected person's meetings. This needs normal Marketplace review and a clear action explanation.

sources.quote: Different from classic scopes, there are total of 4 actions in granular scopes: read, write, update and delete.
The Marketplace Security Review Team verifies that the app only requests the minimum necessary OAuth scopes required for its functionality.

scopeTiers.need: Create and update the connected person's meetings

scopeTiers.text: Read or send chat messages. This needs normal Marketplace review and should remain optional if chat automation is optional.

sources.quote: Users can select all, some, or no optional permissions during authorization.
The Marketplace Security Review Team verifies that the app only requests the minimum necessary OAuth scopes required for its functionality.

scopeTiers.need: Read and send the connected person's chat messages

scopeTiers.text: Access organization-wide meeting data. An account admin must install and authorize this tier. It needs normal Marketplace review.

sources.quote: The user adding the app must be an account admin or owner in order to be granted admin capabilities.
Admin-managed: Account admins add and manage the app. Depending on the scope, the app can access and manage the user data of users on their account.

scopeTiers.need: Read meetings across a customer's organization

essentials.text: User access tokens last 3,600 seconds. Refresh tokens expire after 90 days and rotate. Store each replacement token before using it again.

sources.quote: "refresh_token": "<JWT_TOKEN>", "expires_in": 3600,
Refresh tokens expire after 90 days.
You should always use the latest refresh token for the next refresh request.

essentials.text: Configure an OAuth redirect URL and OAuth allow list. Enable Strict Mode for production callbacks. Do not use loopback or development URLs in production.

sources.quote: OAuth redirect URL (required)
OAuth allow lists (required)
Strict Mode URL (Optional) : Allows only exact matches of the registered OAuth redirect URLs.
While you can use loopback URLs and other development endpoints for development redirects, avoid using them in production redirects.

essentials.text: Expect compliance review before security testing. Zoom checks OWASP Top 10 risks and least-privilege scopes. Encrypt Zoom data in transit and at rest.

Apps are tested against the OWASP Top 10 risks
Encrypt data in transit with modern and standard encryption methods. Encrypt any stored Zoom data when stored

requests.text: Open this browser URL and validate that the returned state matches RANDOM_STATE.

sources.quote: https://zoom.us/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=ZOOM_PUBLIC_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256

Optionally, add a state parameter to the authorization URL. Zoom returns the same state value on the redirect, so your app can confirm that the response matches its request and prevent cross-site request forgery.

detail.text: In Marketplace, open Develop, then Build an app. Create a General app and choose user-managed access. This gives each customer control over their own connection.

sources.quote: On the app creation screen, select General app and click Create.
User-managed: Individual users add and manage the app. The app has access to only the user's authorized data.

steps.title: Confirm developer access

detail.text: Use an account owner, account admin, or assigned developer role. Ask your Zoom account owner to assign the role if needed.

sources.quote: You are either the Zoom account owner, account admin, or have been assigned the Zoom for developers role.

steps.output: A Zoom account with developer permission.

steps.title: Choose external distribution

detail.text: Choose unlisted if you will share the install link yourself. Choose public only if Marketplace search matters. Do not choose private or beta for unrelated customers.

sources.quote: Private apps are intended for distribution to users within your Zoom account.
We don't allow beta apps to be published to the Zoom Marketplace, and we allow beta app access only to members of the developer's Zoom account.

steps.output: Unlisted external distribution, or public distribution.

steps.title: Set callback URLs

detail.text: In OAuth settings, add your HTTPS callback URL and allow-list entry. Enable Strict Mode for production. Use only domains your company controls.

sources.quote: OAuth allow lists (required)
Strict Mode URL (Optional) : Allows only exact matches of the registered OAuth redirect URLs.

steps.output: Production callback URL, allow list, and Strict Mode setting.

steps.title: Draft OAuth callback logic

detail.text: For a web-based agent, use a backend confidential OAuth client. Keep the client secret on the backend and never send it from a browser. Generate a random state for each connection, store it server-side with the user and an expiry, and validate it when Zoom redirects back. Exchange the authorization code from the backend, then atomically replace the stored refresh token. Use PKCE only for a native or other public client that has no backend server.

sources.quote: Zoom returns the same state value on the redirect, so your app can confirm that the response matches its request and prevent cross-site request forgery
A browser call exposes your client secret and fails with a CORS error.

steps.output: Generate a random state per connection. Store it server-side with the user and expiry. Redirect to https://zoom.us/oauth/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, and state. On return, compare state before POSTing the code to https://zoom.us/oauth/token from your backend. Atomically replace the stored refresh token.

steps.title: Select minimum scopes

detail.text: Request only the scopes required by enabled features. Do not combine ordinary user scopes with admin scopes unless the product truly needs organization-wide features and an account admin or owner will authorize them. Make chat and other advanced features optional. Verify the exact current granular scope identifiers in Zoom before configuring them, because the researched sources do not establish the identifiers shown elsewhere in this guide.

sources.quote: Users can select all, some, or no optional permissions during authorization.
The user adding the app must be an account admin or owner in order to be granted admin capabilities.

steps.output: A feature-to-scope list in the app configuration.

steps.title: Test with development credentials

detail.text: Use development credentials while building. Test consent, callback state checks, code exchange, refresh rotation, and expired-refresh reconnection.

sources.quote: Use development credentials while you are building and testing your app.
If your refresh token expires, you can direct the user to the authorize URL to restart the User OAuth flow.

steps.output: Working development connection and test checklist.

steps.title: Add account-level throttling

detail.text: Throttle requests separately for every connected Zoom account. Back off and retry safely after HTTP 429. Do not pool one customer's quota with another customer's work.

sources.quote: These rate limits are shared by users for all apps installed on the account.
When you exceed a rate limit, the API request will fail and return a HTTP 429 status code.

steps.output: Per-account queue, backoff, and HTTP 429 handling.

steps.title: Draft reviewer test plan

detail.text:
Use this as the starting test plan. Replace placeholders with your URL, test credentials, enabled features, and the actions your app actually requests permission to perform. Cover every supported role.

Test plan:
1. Sign in with the supplied test account.
2. Open Connect Zoom and approve only the listed scopes.
3. Perform each enabled action, such as reading meetings or creating a meeting when meeting creation is enabled.
4. Confirm the expected result in Zoom.
5. Revoke access and confirm requests stop.
Roles: standard user and account admin, if admin features exist.
Known limits: no chat automation unless enabled.

sources.quote: To facilitate a smooth review process, provide test credentials that allow Zoom reviewers to fully experience your integration.
A test plan is required for each submission, including re-submissions.

steps.output:
Test plan:
1. Sign in with the supplied test account.
2. Open Connect Zoom and approve only listed scopes.
3. Create a meeting from the agent.
4. Confirm the meeting appears in Zoom.
5. Revoke access and confirm requests stop.
Roles: standard user and account admin, if admin features exist.
Known limits: no chat automation unless enabled.

steps.title: Verify company domains

detail.text: Verify each company-owned domain used in app links and callbacks before submitting. This includes the callback, home, terms, privacy, and webhook URLs that your app uses.

sources.quote: We perform a one-time verification to make sure that the domain where you receive Zoom callbacks is owned by you.

steps.output: Verified domains for callback, home, terms, privacy, and webhook URLs.

steps.title: Prepare security materials

detail.text: Document where Zoom data moves, where it is stored, and when it is deleted. Describe encryption and third-party model processing. Keep requested scopes tied to documented features.

sources.quote: Confirm that any third party with whom your app shares Personal User Data will provide the same or equal protection of Personal User Data as required in Zoom's developer guidelines.
Encrypt data in transit with modern and standard encryption methods. Encrypt any stored Zoom data when stored

steps.output: Technical design, architecture, data-flow, retention, deletion, and security-control documents.

steps.title: Submit production app

detail.text: Submit the public or unlisted app for Marketplace review. Run first-time authorization with the Production Client ID. Include reviewer credentials and the test plan.

sources.quote: For First-time submissions Make sure your environment is using the Production Client ID during authorization.
Public and unlisted apps undergo a dedicated review process.

steps.output: Marketplace review submission with production authorization, test credentials, and test plan.

detail.text: Zoom performs functionality, compliance, and security review. Initial responses are stated within five business days. Community guidance says security review can take about two weeks.

sources.quote: The app review submission response time is within 5 business days.
Once the functional review is passed you continue to security review which can take 2 weeks give or take depending on the quality of information provided in the TDD documentation provided.

steps.title: Publish the approved app

detail.text: Publish the approved app or share its unlisted install link. Let each customer authorize their own account. Explain any optional permissions before consent.

sources.quote: Unlisted apps might be a preferable option for you if you want to limit access to your app and don't want it available to the general public.

steps.output: Public listing or unlisted install link.

steps.title: Add webhook verification

detail.text: If you use webhooks, verify x-zm-signature using your secret token. Do not allow-list Zoom IP addresses. Monitor endpoint health because repeated failed checks disable subscriptions.

sources.quote: Zoom uses the value of the secret token to hash the webhook data, which it sends in the x-zm-signature webhook request header.
We strongly recommend that you Verify webhook events instead of creating an allow list of Zoom IP addresses because Zoom may update the IP ranges used at any time.
If the revalidation check fails 6 times in a row, Zoom will stop sending webhook events and disable the event subscription.

steps.output: HTTPS webhook endpoint with HMAC-SHA-256 signature verification and monitoring.

gotchas.text: Do not use Server-to-Server OAuth for customer connections. It has account authorization and no user consent refresh cycle.

sources.quote: Access tokens expire after one hour. After your access token expires, you can request a new one. Zoom does not require a separate refresh flow.

gotchas.text: A customer's Marketplace administrator can block a user's authorization until they pre-approve the app.

sources.quote: A Zoom account may require an app be pre-approved by a Marketplace admin before the end user may authorize it.

gotchas.text: Do not train, evaluate, or improve language models with Zoom Customer Content without Zoom's express written permission.

sources.quote: You may not use any Customer Content ... to train, develop, evaluate, test, improve, or modify artificial intelligence or machine learning models (including language models)

gotchas.text: Refresh tokens rotate. Concurrent refresh attempts can lose the newest token unless replacement storage is atomic.

sources.quote: You should always use the latest refresh token for the next refresh request.

whenBlocked.text: If a customer cannot authorize, ask their Zoom Marketplace administrator to pre-approve the app for that account.

sources.quote: A Zoom account may require an app be pre-approved by a Marketplace admin before the end user may authorize it.

whenBlocked.text: If review stalls or a rejection is unclear, reply in Marketplace review notes and email integration.testers@zoom.us.

sources.quote: You can reach out to us if you have any questions or concerns at integration.testers@zoom.us .

whenBlocked.text: If a refresh token expires, send the affected customer through the Zoom authorization flow again.

sources.quote: If your refresh token expires, you can direct the user to the authorize URL to restart the User OAuth flow.

whenBlocked.text: If webhook delivery stops, restore the endpoint and recreate the disabled event subscription.

sources.quote: If the revalidation check fails 6 times in a row, Zoom will stop sending webhook events and disable the event subscription.

uncertain: The sources do not state test-user limits or development-app limits.
The sources do not state the cost of a normal Marketplace OAuth app.
The sources do not provide exact granular scope identifiers for each meeting and chat capability.
The 2–3 week review estimate combines Zoom's five-business-day initial response with a community-reported security-review duration.
